purpose: Pin the byte-level wire behaviour of the asyncio Python SDK. This file is PURE DATA: it is written before any implementation code and must never import the SDK.
precedence: Where astral-docs and astral-go/the live node disagree, the live node and astral-go win. Every such disagreement is recorded in the affected vector's notes and in the corpus report.

source_kinds.doc-literal: the hex appears verbatim in astral-docs; ref names the file and section
source_kinds.go-derived: produced by executing astral-go's own encoder at HEAD 5c18d9c; ref names the file and function
source_kinds.live: captured off the wire from the running node; ref names the probe

negative_vectors.description: a presence/nil flag byte in the range 0x02..0xff
negative_vectors.ref: topics/binary-encoding.md § Presence flag values; corroborated by astral-go@5c18d9c astral/ptr_value.go ptrValue.ReadFrom ("invalid nil flag")
negative_vectors.notes: the doc tabulates `02 .. ff  any other - rejected as corrupt`; the byte shown here stands for that whole range. A conformant reader rejects the flag itself, before reading any value bytes.

negative_vectors.description: 0x00 in a slice element's synthesised presence slot
negative_vectors.notes: DOCS DISAGREE: topics/binary-encoding.md presents 0x00 as a legal 'absent' value everywhere, but a value-kind slot has no absent state and astral-go accepts ONLY 0x01. 0x00 is legal only for a POINTER-kind element.

negative_vectors.notes: the 4 bytes are consumed before validation, so the stream is unrecoverable

negative_vectors.description: parsing the JSON value "" as an ObjectID
negative_vectors.notes: astral-go MARSHALS the zero ObjectID to "" but cannot PARSE it back. A Python port should accept "" as the zero ID on input while still emitting "" for bug-compatibility, and must not rely on a JSON round trip.

negative_vectors.description: encoding a non-nil polymorphic value whose ObjectType() is empty
negative_vectors.notes: DOCS DISAGREE: topics/codec.md says only the Canonical encoder rejects an empty type; ShortTypeEncoder rejects it too. Untyped blobs on a binary channel bypass the codec entirely.

negative_vectors.ref: astral-go@5c18d9c astral/string_types.go String8.WriteTo ("string8: data too large")

negative_vectors.description: a map whose key kind is Go's platform-width int/uint
negative_vectors.notes: key kinds are closed: string (encoded string16) or uint8/16/32/64. Python must require an explicit width so content hashes never depend on the host.

gaps.want: live captures of blueprint sync, services.discover, objects.create/read, tree, crypto, auth, user, nodes and exonet payloads
gaps.why: The live node's apphost request path is wedged. It still ACCEPTS connections and pushes the host_info_msg greeting on tcp:8625, unix:~/.apphost.sock and ws://127.0.0.1:8624/.ws, but never answers any inbound message on any of the three: route_query_msg, a deliberately malformed top-level message and register_service_msg all time out. `ss -ltn` shows the 8625 listener with 36 connections stuck in the accept backlog and ~36 half-closed sessions in CLOSE-WAIT. The HTTP surface on :8624 still answers (401 without a bearer token), so the process is alive; only apphost request handling is stalled. The node was left untouched as instructed.

gaps.want: doc-literal vectors for the remaining ~35 primitive and composite types
gaps.why: astral-docs contains exactly nine hex code blocks in total (topics/codec.md and topics/binary-encoding.md) plus one in primitive-types/object.md. Every other primitive-type page is prose only. Everything else here is necessarily go-derived or live.

gaps.want: the authoritative JSON shape of a polymorphic (astral.Object) struct field
gaps.why: Two candidate shapes exist and no live capture could settle it. Compiled Go structs marshal through encoding/json, so a polymorphic field renders as the inner object's own JSON (vector struct.demo: "Any":"1122334455667788"). The blueprint/RuntimeObject JSON path is expected to emit the JSONAdapter envelope {"Type":...,"Object":...} instead. survey-go-core.md §8 asserts the envelope form; running astral-go produced the inline form. Resolve against a live node or a RuntimeObject probe before implementing.

gaps.want: the authoritative JSON shape of a bare []byte struct field
gaps.why: survey-go-core.md §12.11 says a plain []byte field marshals as a JSON array of numbers. Running astral-go's own struct marshalling produced base64 (vector struct.demo: "Raw":"3q0="), because encoding/json handles []byte before any astral code runs. The number-array claim presumably belongs to the reflection/RuntimeObject path. Unresolved; the BINARY form is unambiguous and is pinned by struct.plain_bytes_is_uint8_slice.

gaps.want: a vector for the Indexed type encoder
gaps.why: Indexed encoding is a uint8 index into a closed table both parties agreed on out of band. There is no table in the docs and none in astral-go's defaults, so no vector can be pinned without inventing one.

These live inside an established Noise XK link between two nodes. topics/link-mux.md gives field lists but no bytes, astral-go's frame types were not exercised, and no second node is reachable. Tier 3 anyway. The doc also never states whether relay_query's identity fields carry a pointer presence byte.

gaps.want: a vector for a full blueprint sync exchange
gaps.why: Individual astral.blueprint* objects are pinned here, but the SYNC protocol (dependency ordering, replay, conflict detection by Object ID) is a multi-message flow that needs a live peer.

gaps.want: vectors for string64/bytes64 near their 2^64-1 cap
gaps.why: Not representable. What matters for the port is the allocation cap, which is a decoder policy rather than an encoding; see neg.string8.oversize for the shape of the write-side check.

gaps.want: a vector emitted with the ':' base64 separator by astral-go's text sender
gaps.why: astral-go's TextSender emits ' ' whenever the object implements MarshalText, and Blob does, so it never emits '#[]:<base64>'. The ':' form appears only on the PARSE side and in the live out=text capture of dir.alias_map (which is pinned as live.dir_alias_map's text field, and is the only ':' example in the corpus).

gaps.want: confirmation that zone 0x00 really JSON-marshals to ""
gaps.why: Produced by astral-go (vector zone.none) but documented nowhere: core-definitions/zone.md gives no JSON encoding at all and there is no primitive-types/zone.md. Parsing "" yields 0x00, not the 0x07 default, so the round trip holds - but the docs are silent.
